source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י׀קִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֗ים וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֹת֔וֹ אֶל־בֵּ֥ית אֲבִינָדָ֖ב בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְאֶת־אֶלְעָזָ֤ר בְּנוֹ֙ קִדְּשׁ֔וּ לִשְׁמֹ֖ר אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] men of Kiriath-jearim and brought up [the] ark of Yahweh, and brought it to [the] house of Abinadab on the hill; and Eleazar his son they consecrated to keep [the] ark of Yahweh.

en.L: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They brought it to the hilltop house of Abinadab, and they consecrated Eleazar his son to keep watch over the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and carried the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to their town. They took it to the house of a man named Abinadab, which stood on the hill. They set apart Abinadab's son Eleazar for the holy work of guarding the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the men of Kiriath-jearim came: the answer to the request of 6:21
decisions.reason: The people of Beth-shemesh, after the deaths among them (6:19-20), had sent to Kiriath-jearim asking its people to come and take the ark up. The town lay higher in the hill country, so the ark is "brought up" from the valley of Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: on the hill: a hill in or by the town
decisions.reason: The word means "hill". It probably points to the high part of Kiriath-jearim where Abinadab lived, and 2 Samuel 6:3-4 uses the same words when David moves the ark from there. It is not the town of Gibeah, Saul's home, which is spelled the same way but lay elsewhere.

decisions.choice: consecrated him to keep the ark: set him apart for the holy duty of guarding it
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to set apart for God's service. "Keep" is the verb used for the Levites' duty of guarding the holy things (Numbers 3:7-8, 28, 32). The text does not say whether Abinadab's family were Levites; it says only that Eleazar was made holy for this task, so that the ark was cared for and not treated carelessly as at Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: carried ... up to their town; for the holy work of guarding
decisions.reason: Readable says where the ark was taken and explains "consecrated" as being set apart for holy work. Balanced keeps "consecrated" and says "keep watch over" for the duty that Literal calls "keep".

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִיּ֞וֹם שֶׁ֤בֶת הָֽאָרוֹן֙ בְּקִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֔ים וַיִּרְבּוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּנָּה֛וּ כָּל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, from [the] day [the] ark dwelt in Kiriath-jearim, and were many the days, and they were twenty years; and lamented all [the] house of Israel after Yahweh.

en.L: And it happened that from the day the ark stayed in Kiriath-jearim, the days became many, and they were twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: From the day the ark came to stay in Kiriath-jearim, a long time went by, twenty years in all, and the whole house of Israel mourned and longed for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The ark stayed in Kiriath-jearim for a long time, twenty years. All through those years, the people of Israel mourned and longed for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: lamented after the LORD: mourned in longing for the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; it means to wail or lament (Micah 2:4; Ezekiel 32:18). With "after" it seems to describe grief that reaches out toward the LORD: the people mourned his absence and longed for him. The ancient Greek translation has "looked back after the Lord", which may rest on a slightly different word, and some take the sense to be "turned after" or "gathered after" the LORD. Whichever reading is right, verses 3-6 show Israel turning back to him.

decisions.choice: twenty years: the time until Samuel's call to return in verse 3
decisions.reason: The ark stayed at Kiriath-jearim much longer, until David brought it to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:2-3; 1 Chronicles 13:5-6). The twenty years measure the time from the ark's arrival to the turning point that follows, when Samuel calls the people back.

decisions.choice: the days became many: a long time passed
decisions.reason: A common way of saying that much time went by (Genesis 38:12).

decisions.choice: mourned and longed for
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use two verbs to carry both sides of the phrase: grief, and grief directed toward the LORD. Literal keeps the bare "lamented after".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֶל־כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם־בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֤ם שָׁבִים֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה הָסִ֜ירוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֧י הַנֵּכָ֛ר מִתּוֹכְכֶ֖ם וְהָעַשְׁתָּר֑וֹת וְהָכִ֨ינוּ לְבַבְכֶ֤ם אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וְעִבְדֻ֣הוּ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְיַצֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Samuel to all [the] house of Israel, saying, If with all your heart you [are] returning to Yahweh, remove [the] gods of the foreigner from your midst, and the Ashtaroth, and fix your heart to Yahweh and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from [the] hand of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, "If you are returning to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart, remove the foreign gods from among you, and the Ashtaroth, and fix your heart on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."
en.B: Then Samuel said to the whole house of Israel, "If you are coming back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart, get rid of the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth that are among you. Set your hearts firmly on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue you from the power of the Philistines."
en.R: Then Samuel spoke to all the people of Israel. He said, "Are you really coming back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart? Then throw away the gods of other nations and the goddesses called the Ashtaroth that you keep among you. Set your hearts on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worship only {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue you from the Philistines."

decisions.choice: if you are returning with all your heart: a test of whether the turning is real
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a turning already under way, the mourning of verse 2. Samuel does not deny it; he says what a true return must look like. A return "with all the heart" is shown by what is put away and by whom the people serve.

decisions.choice: the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth: the gods and goddesses of Canaan and its neighbors
decisions.reason: Ashtaroth is the plural of Ashtoreth, a Canaanite goddess of fertility and war; the plural takes in her many local forms. With the Baals of verse 4 she stands for the whole of Canaanite religion, as in Judges 2:13 and 10:6. "Remove the foreign gods" repeats Jacob's command to his household (Genesis 35:2) and Joshua's charge (Joshua 24:23), and what Israel did in Judges 10:16.

decisions.choice: fix your heart on the LORD: set your will on him firmly and steadily
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or set in place. Applied to the heart it means a settled decision, not a passing mood; Psalm 78:8 uses it of a generation that "did not set its heart firmly".

decisions.choice: serve him alone, and he will deliver you: the rescue comes from the LORD himself
decisions.reason: The service owed to the LORD is undivided, as the first commandment requires (Exodus 20:3; Deuteronomy 6:13). Samuel promises rescue from the LORD, not from the ark or an army. Twenty years earlier Israel had fetched the ark to save them in battle, and it was lost (4:3-11).

decisions.choice: Are you really ...? Then ...; the gods of other nations; the goddesses called the Ashtaroth; worship
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long condition into a question and an answer, says plainly that the "foreign gods" are the gods of other peoples, and explains who the Ashtaroth were, as Judges 2:13 does. It says "worship" for "serve" here, as Judges does.

decisions.choice: rescue ... from the power of the Philistines (Balanced); rescue ... from the Philistines (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Balanced turns "hand" into "power", and Readable drops the picture. Literal keeps "deliver" and "hand".

source.text: וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־הָעַשְׁתָּרֹ֑ת וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And removed [the] sons of Israel the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and they served Yahweh alone.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone.
en.B: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} got rid of the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone.
en.R: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} got rid of their idols of Baal and of the goddesses called the Ashtaroth. They worshiped only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Baals and the Ashtaroth: the gods and goddesses of Canaan
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god, worshiped under many local names, so the plural means the Baal gods of many places; the Ashtaroth are explained at verse 3. To remove them means to destroy or throw out their images and the objects used to worship them (Genesis 35:4; Judges 10:16).

decisions.choice: removed ... served the LORD alone: Samuel's words carried out exactly
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the two verbs of Samuel's command in verse 3, "remove" and "serve him alone". The people do what he said, word for word.

decisions.choice: their idols of Baal and of the goddesses called the Ashtaroth
decisions.reason: Readable says that what was removed were idols, and explains the Ashtaroth as at verse 3.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל קִבְצ֥וּ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וְאֶתְפַּלֵּ֥ל בַּעַדְכֶ֖ם אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Samuel, Gather all Israel to the Mizpah, and I will pray for you to Yahweh.

en.L: And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Then Samuel said, "Bring all Israel together at Mizpah, and I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for you."
en.R: Then Samuel said, "Bring all the people of Israel together at Mizpah. I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for you there."

decisions.choice: Mizpah: a town in Benjamin where the tribes gathered
decisions.reason: The name means "lookout". This Mizpah lay in the land of Benjamin, a few miles north of Jerusalem, and served as a meeting place for all Israel (Judges 20:1; 1 Samuel 10:17). It is not the Mizpah in Gilead (Judges 10:17).

decisions.choice: I will pray for you: Samuel stands between the people and God
decisions.reason: Like Moses (Exodus 32:11-14; Numbers 21:7), Samuel prays for the people. Later he says that to stop praying for them would be a sin against the LORD (12:23), and Jeremiah 15:1 and Psalm 99:6 name Moses and Samuel together as those who prayed for Israel.

decisions.choice: and I will pray: the purpose of the gathering
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses intention: gather the people, so that I may pray for you. The gathering at Mizpah is for prayer, not for war.

decisions.choice: there
decisions.reason: Readable adds "there" to make clear that the prayer will take place at the gathering.

source.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ הַ֠מִּצְפָּתָה וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ־מַ֜יִם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכ֣וּ׀לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּצ֨וּמוּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ שָׁ֔ם חָטָ֖אנוּ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֧ט שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gathered to the Mizpah and drew water and poured [it] out before Yahweh, and they fasted on that day and said there, We have sinned against Yahweh. And judged Samuel [the] sons of Israel at the Mizpah.

en.L: And they gathered at Mizpah and drew water and poured [it] out before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they fasted on that day and said there, "We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And Samuel judged the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel at Mizpah.
en.B: After gathering at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They fasted that day and confessed there, "We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." It was at Mizpah that Samuel judged the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: So the people gathered at Mizpah. They drew water and poured it out on the ground before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That day they went without food, and there they said, "We have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." At Mizpah, Samuel led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: drew water and poured it out before the LORD: an act of repentance
alternatives: a sign of grief and helplessness
a heart poured out in prayer
decisions.reason: This rite is found nowhere else, and the text does not explain it. Water poured on the ground cannot be gathered up again (2 Samuel 14:14), so it may picture helplessness and grief, or a heart poured out before God (Lamentations 2:19; Psalm 62:9). It may also be an offering given up wholly, as when David poured out water before the LORD (2 Samuel 23:16). Joined here to fasting and confession, it belongs to the people's repentance.

decisions.choice: fasted ... said, We have sinned: the outward signs of repentance
decisions.reason: Fasting went with grief and with seeking God's mercy (Judges 20:26; Joel 2:12). The people say plainly what they have done. Their confession answers the call of verse 3.

decisions.choice: Samuel judged: led and governed Israel as a judge
decisions.reason: This is the verb used of the judges whom the LORD raised up to rescue and lead Israel (Judges 2:16-18), and of Eli (4:18). Here it may include settling the people's matters before God as they turned back, and it opens the account of Samuel as the last of the judges (verses 15-17).

decisions.choice: confessed
decisions.reason: Balanced says "confessed" for "said", since what they said was a confession of sin.

decisions.choice: on the ground; went without food; led
decisions.reason: Readable says where the water was poured and explains fasting. As in Judges, it says "led" for "judged", so that a new reader does not picture only a court; Literal and Balanced keep "judged".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים כִּֽי־הִתְקַבְּצ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּצְפָּ֔תָה וַיַּעֲל֥וּ סַרְנֵֽי־פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] Philistines that had gathered [the] sons of Israel to the Mizpah, and went up [the] rulers of [the] Philistines against Israel; and heard [the] sons of Israel and were afraid from before [the] Philistines.

en.L: And the Philistines heard that the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel. And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel heard [it] and were afraid of the Philistines.
en.B: When the Philistines heard that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had gathered at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines marched up against Israel. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard about it and were afraid of the Philistines.
en.R: The Philistines heard that the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had come together at Mizpah. So the Philistine rulers led their troops up to attack Israel. When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard about this, they were afraid of the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (Joshua 13:3; Judges 16:5; 1 Samuel 6:16-18). They act together here, as they did in sending back the ark.

decisions.choice: they heard ... and went up: the gathering was taken as a threat
decisions.reason: A gathering of all the tribes was how Israel prepared for war (Judges 20:1-2), so the Philistines probably took the assembly at Mizpah as the start of a revolt and moved to crush it. The people, however, had gathered to pray, and they had no army ready.

decisions.choice: afraid of the Philistines: "from before", because of their approach
decisions.reason: The phrase means fear caused by the Philistines and their coming. The memory of the defeat at Ebenezer (4:10) lay behind it.

decisions.choice: led their troops up to attack
decisions.reason: Readable says what "went up against" means: the rulers came with their forces to fight.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אַל־תַּחֲרֵ֣שׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ מִזְּעֹ֖ק אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵ֖נוּ מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] sons of Israel to Samuel, Do not keep silent from us from crying out to Yahweh our God, and he will save us from [the] hand of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not keep silent from us, from crying out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us from the power of the Philistines."
en.R: They begged Samuel, "Please keep on calling out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for us! Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us from the Philistines."

decisions.choice: do not keep silent from us, from crying out: do not stop praying aloud for us
decisions.reason: To "keep silent from" someone is to stop speaking for them or to them (Psalm 28:1). The people hold Samuel to his promise in verse 5: they ask him to keep calling out to God on their behalf while the enemy comes.

decisions.choice: save us: now Israel looks to the LORD in prayer
decisions.reason: In 4:3 the elders sent for the ark, so that it might save them from the Philistines. Now, facing the same enemy, they ask for prayer to "the LORD our God". The verb form expresses the hoped-for result: that he may save them.

decisions.choice: They begged Samuel, "Please keep on ...!"
decisions.reason: Readable puts the negative command in positive form and shows the urgency of the request with "begged" and "please"; the sense is the same: do not stop.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל טְלֵ֤ה חָלָב֙ אֶחָ֔ד וַיַּעֲלֵ֧הוּ עוֹלָ֛ה כָּלִ֖יל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּזְעַ֨ק שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בְּעַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Samuel a lamb of milk, one, and offered it up [as] a burnt offering, whole, to Yahweh; and cried out Samuel to Yahweh for Israel, and answered him Yahweh.

en.L: And Samuel took one milk lamb and offered it up [as] a burnt offering, whole, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and Samuel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for Israel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him.
en.B: Then Samuel took a young lamb that was still nursing and offered it whole as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for Israel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him.
en.R: Then Samuel took a young lamb that was still drinking its mother's milk, and he offered the whole lamb to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a burnt offering. Samuel cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for Israel, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him.

decisions.choice: a milk lamb: a lamb still suckling
decisions.reason: The phrase means a lamb not yet weaned. The law allowed such young animals to be offered from the eighth day after birth (Leviticus 22:27). Samuel offers what is at hand, one small lamb, for the whole people.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering, whole: an offering burned entirely, nothing kept back
decisions.reason: Every burnt offering was burned on the altar, but the added word "whole" stresses that all of it went up to the LORD (Leviticus 6:15-16; Deuteronomy 33:10). The offering expresses the people's complete surrender.

decisions.choice: offered it up (the reading the scribes marked)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "and he offered up" with no object; the reading the scribes marked (qere) adds "it". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the LORD answered him: the prayer of verse 8 is heard
decisions.reason: Samuel does what the people asked: he cries out to the LORD. The answer is not told in words; the next verse shows it in the LORD's thunder against the Philistines.

decisions.choice: a young lamb that was still nursing (Balanced); still drinking its mother's milk (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the short Hebrew phrase "milk lamb"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י שְׁמוּאֵל֙ מַעֲלֶ֣ה הָעוֹלָ֔ה וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים נִגְּשׁ֔וּ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּרְעֵ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה׀בְּקוֹל־גָּ֠דוֹל בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא עַל־פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ וַיְהֻמֵּ֔ם וַיִּנָּגְפ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, Samuel [was] offering up the burnt offering, and [the] Philistines drew near for battle against Israel; and thundered Yahweh with a great sound on that day against [the] Philistines and confused them, and they were struck before Israel.

en.L: And it happened, while Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, that the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thundered with a great sound on that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were struck down before Israel.
en.B: Samuel was in the middle of offering up the burnt offering when the Philistines drew near to attack Israel. But that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thundered against the Philistines with a mighty roar and threw them into panic, and they were beaten before Israel.
en.R: Samuel was still offering the burnt offering when the Philistines came close to fight against Israel. But that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent a great crash of thunder against the Philistines. It threw them into panic, and they lost the battle to Israel.

decisions.choice: while Samuel was offering: the attack and the answer come during the offering
decisions.reason: The verb form shows the offering still going on when the Philistines come near. Israel takes no action of its own; the turn of the battle comes from the LORD while the priestly act and the prayer are under way (verse 9).

decisions.choice: thundered with a great sound: a mighty peal of thunder
decisions.reason: The word for "sound" is also the word for "voice", and thunder is often called the LORD's voice (Exodus 9:23; Psalm 29:3). The storm is the LORD's own answer.

decisions.choice: the LORD thundered against the Philistines: Hannah's words come true
decisions.reason: Hannah sang that the LORD would shatter his enemies: "against them he thunders in the heavens" (2:10). The same verb is used here, in the first victory of her son's leadership.

decisions.choice: threw them into confusion: panic sent by the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb describes the panic the LORD sends on Israel's enemies in battle, so that they cannot stand (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10; Judges 4:15).

decisions.choice: a mighty roar; panic; beaten (Balanced); lost the battle to Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "panic" for the sudden terror the verb describes, and Readable puts the passive "were struck down before Israel" as a plain statement of who won. Literal keeps "with a great sound".

source.text: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִן־הַמִּצְפָּ֔ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּכּ֕וּם עַד־מִתַּ֖חַת לְבֵ֥ית כָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] men of Israel from the Mizpah and pursued [the] Philistines and struck them as far as below Beth-car.

en.L: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.
en.B: The men of Israel went out from Mizpah, chased the Philistines, and struck them down all the way to a place below Beth-car.
en.R: The men of Israel went out from Mizpah and chased the Philistines. They kept attacking them all the way to the land below the town of Beth-car.

decisions.choice: went out ... pursued ... struck: Israel follows up the LORD's victory
decisions.reason: The men of Israel act only after the LORD has routed the enemy (verse 10). Their part is the pursuit.

decisions.choice: below Beth-car: a place west of Mizpah, now unknown
decisions.reason: Beth-car is named only here. "Below" suggests a point lower down the slopes, on the way from the hills toward the Philistine plain.

decisions.choice: the town of Beth-car
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so that the name is not taken for a person, as it does with other place names.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶ֣בֶן אַחַ֗ת וַיָּ֤שֶׂם בֵּֽין־הַמִּצְפָּה֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַשֵּׁ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמָ֖הּ אֶ֣בֶן הָעָ֑זֶר וַיֹּאמַ֕ר עַד־הֵ֖נָּה עֲזָרָ֥נוּ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Samuel a stone, one, and set [it] between the Mizpah and between the Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, and said, Until here has helped us Yahweh.

en.L: And Samuel took one stone and set [it] between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, and said, "As far as this {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has helped us."
en.B: Then Samuel took a single stone and placed it between Mizpah and Shen. He called it Ebenezer and said, "To this point {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has helped us."
en.R: Then Samuel took a stone and stood it up between Mizpah and Shen. He gave it the name Ebenezer, which means "stone of help". He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has helped us all the way to this point."

decisions.choice: Ebenezer: "the stone of help"
decisions.reason: The name is made of the word for "stone" and the word for "help". Samuel explains it himself: "the LORD has helped us". The stone is a witness to what the LORD did, as stones set up by Jacob and by Joshua were (Genesis 28:18-22; Joshua 4:6-7; 24:26-27).

decisions.choice: Ebenezer: the name of the place of Israel's earlier defeat
decisions.reason: Twenty years before, Israel had camped at a place called Ebenezer, near Aphek, when it was beaten and the ark was taken (4:1; 5:1). That place seems to lie farther west than this stone between Mizpah and Shen, so the two may not be the same spot. Either way, the name that recalled defeat and the loss of the ark now marks the LORD's help.

decisions.choice: Shen: the place name of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the Shen", which means "the tooth" and may name a sharp crag. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "Jeshanah", a town north of Mizpah (2 Chronicles 13:19), which differs from it by one letter. The Hebrew reading is kept; the place is unknown either way.

decisions.choice: as far as this: both to this place and to this time
decisions.reason: The word usually means "to here", of a place, but can also mean "until now", of time. Here both fit: the LORD has helped Israel all the way to this battlefield, and all the way to this day.

decisions.choice: Ebenezer (Readable adds: which means "stone of help")
decisions.reason: The name is kept at every level, since it is the name the place bore and the one used at 4:1 and 5:1. Readable gives its meaning so that the reader can see how Samuel's words explain it.

decisions.choice: to this point
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose words that can refer to place or to time, as the Hebrew can (m4).

source.text: וַיִּכָּֽנְעוּ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְלֹא־יָסְפ֣וּ ע֔וֹד לָב֖וֹא בִּגְב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתְּהִ֤י יַד־יְהוָה֙ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And were subdued the Philistines, and not they again came into [the] territory of Israel; and was [the] hand of Yahweh against [the] Philistines all [the] days of Samuel.

en.L: And the Philistines were subdued and did not again come into the territory of Israel; and the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
en.B: So the Philistines were brought low, and they did not invade Israel's territory again. The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was against the Philistines throughout the days of Samuel.
en.R: So the Philistines were defeated, and they did not come into Israel's land again. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power against the Philistines all through Samuel's time.

decisions.choice: the Philistines were subdued: the words that close a judge's victory
decisions.reason: The same verb ends the stories of Ehud, Deborah, Gideon and Jephthah (Judges 3:30; 4:23; 8:28; 11:33). Samuel's victory is told as the last of the great rescues of the judges.

decisions.choice: did not come again ... all the days of Samuel: no further invasion while Samuel led Israel
decisions.reason: Later chapters tell of Philistine garrisons and wars in Saul's time (10:5; 13:3-5; 14:52), while Samuel was still alive. The words are best taken as a summary of Samuel's own leadership before the king, when the Philistines no longer marched into Israel's land as they had before. Some take "all the days of Samuel" as his whole life, meaning the LORD kept the Philistines in check throughout, even when they fought Israel.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines: the LORD's power at work against them
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The LORD's hand had been heavy on the Philistine cities while they held the ark (5:6, 9, 11); now it is against them in battle.

decisions.choice: used his power against
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand. Balanced keeps the phrase, which reads naturally.

source.text: וַתָּשֹׁ֣בְנָה הֶעָרִ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָֽקְחוּ־פְלִשְׁתִּים֩ מֵאֵ֨ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל׀לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעֶקְר֣וֹן וְעַד־גַּ֔ת וְאֶ֨ת־גְּבוּלָ֔ן הִצִּ֥יל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם בֵּ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned the cities which had taken [the] Philistines from Israel to Israel, from Ekron and to Gath; and their territory delivered Israel from [the] hand of [the] Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and between the Amorite.

en.L: And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel returned to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath, and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
en.B: The towns that the Philistines had taken from Israel were given back to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and Israel freed the land around them from the power of the Philistines. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
en.R: Israel got back the towns that the Philistines had taken from them, the towns from Ekron to Gath. Israel also freed the land around those towns from the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

decisions.choice: from Ekron to Gath: the towns along the border between those two cities
decisions.reason: Ekron and Gath were two of the five Philistine cities, and they stayed Philistine (17:52; 27:2). The towns returned were Israelite towns in the land toward them, on the edge of the coastal plain.

decisions.choice: their territory: the land belonging to those towns
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to the towns. Israel took back not only the towns but the fields and villages around them.

decisions.choice: peace with the Amorites: no war with the other peoples of the land
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is used as a general name for the older peoples of Canaan who still lived among and around Israel (Joshua 24:15; Judges 6:10). The singular in the Hebrew speaks of them as one people. With the Philistines held back, Israel had peace on its other borders too.

decisions.choice: Israel got back the towns
decisions.reason: Readable makes Israel the subject, instead of saying that the towns "returned", which is the same event told from Israel's side.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ט שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And judged Samuel Israel all [the] days of his life.

en.L: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
en.B: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
en.R: Samuel led Israel as long as he lived.

decisions.choice: judged: led and governed Israel
decisions.reason: As at verse 6 and in Judges (2:16-18), the verb covers the whole work of leading the people. Verses 16-17 show that it included deciding cases.

decisions.choice: all the days of his life: Samuel's leadership continued after Saul became king
decisions.reason: Samuel goes on guiding Israel, praying for it and rebuking its king after Saul is made king (12:23; 15:1-35), until his death (25:1). This sentence sums up his whole life's work, ahead of the story of the king.

decisions.choice: led
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Readable says "led" for "judged"; Literal and Balanced keep "judged".

source.text: וְהָלַ֗ךְ מִדֵּ֤י שָׁנָה֙ בְּשָׁנָ֔ה וְסָבַב֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְהַגִּלְגָּ֖ל וְהַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְשָׁפַט֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַמְּקוֹמ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went from [the] sufficiency of year in year and went around Bethel and the Gilgal and the Mizpah, and judged Israel all these places.

en.L: And he went year by year and went around [to] Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and judged Israel [in] all these places.
en.B: Every year he would make a round of Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah, judging Israel at each of these places.
en.R: Every year he traveled around to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah, and in each of these places he led Israel and decided their cases.

decisions.choice: from the sufficiency of year in year: every year, year after year
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as often as the year comes round", that is, yearly (Zechariah 14:16). The verbs describe something Samuel did regularly.

decisions.choice: Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah: old places of worship and gathering
decisions.reason: Gilgal was Israel's first camp in the land (Joshua 4:19; 5:9); Bethel was where Jacob met God and where the tribes later sought him (Genesis 28:19; Judges 20:18, 26); Mizpah was the gathering place of verse 5. All three lie within a short distance of Samuel's home at Ramah.

decisions.choice: judged Israel in all these places
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the object marker before "all these places", where a word for "in" would be expected; the sense is clear: he judged Israel at each place on his round.

decisions.choice: led Israel and decided their cases
decisions.reason: Readable says "led" for "judged", as in Judges, and adds "decided their cases" because a regular round of towns shows judging in its ordinary sense of settling disputes.

source.text: וּתְשֻׁבָת֤וֹ הָרָמָ֨תָה֙ כִּֽי־שָׁ֣ם בֵּית֔וֹ וְשָׁ֖ם שָׁפָ֣ט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽבֶן־שָׁ֥ם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And his return [was] to the Ramah, for there [was] his house, and there he judged Israel; and he built there an altar to Yahweh.

en.L: And his return [was] to Ramah, for his house [was] there, and there he judged Israel; and he built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then he would go back to Ramah, since his home was there, and he judged Israel there as well. And he built an altar there to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then he would go back home to Ramah, where he lived, and he led Israel there too. He also built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Ramah.

decisions.choice: Ramah, his home: the town of Samuel's family
decisions.reason: Ramah, "height", is the Ramathaim of 1:1, where Samuel's parents lived (1:19; 2:11). It lay in the hill country north of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: his return was to Ramah: each round ended at home
decisions.reason: The noun phrase, "his return", describes what happened each time: after his round of verse 16 he went back to Ramah.

decisions.choice: he built an altar: worship at Ramah while the ark was away
decisions.reason: The ark stood in a private house at Kiriath-jearim (verse 1), and the sanctuary at Shiloh no longer served as Israel's center after the disaster of chapter 4 (Jeremiah 7:12). Samuel, as the LORD's prophet, built an altar at his home, and the people later worshiped at such places (9:12-13).

decisions.choice: go back home ... led Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Ramah was Samuel's home, and says "led" for "judged" as elsewhere.
